title: Total tensor exactness and K-flatness for a flat-quotient short exact sequence
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and work with sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $0\to L^\bullet\xrightarrow{f}K^\bullet\xrightarrow{g}P^\bullet\to0$ be a sequence of integer-indexed cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] which is short exact in every degree, meaning $f^i$ is monic, $g^i$ is epic, and $\operatorname{im}(f^i)=\ker(g^i)$ for every $i\in\mathbf Z$. Suppose each $P^i$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For every cochain complex $A^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules, the induced sequence of direct-sum total tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]
$$0\to\operatorname{Tot}(L^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}A^\bullet)\xrightarrow{f\otimes1}\operatorname{Tot}(K^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}A^\bullet)\xrightarrow{g\otimes1}\operatorname{Tot}(P^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}A^\bullet)\to0$$
is short exact in every degree. If any two of $L^\bullet,K^\bullet,P^\bullet$ are K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex], then the third is K-flat. No boundedness or degreewise splitting hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: In each degree p, evaluate the given short exact sequence. Convert IsFlatOnSite of the quotient to finite-limit preservation for tensorRight using siteSheafTensorRightIso from [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits]. Run the 03EX proof at independent universes: use the proved public helper SheafOfModules.hasFunctorialFlatResolution_kfi in the module of [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] to choose a flat cover of the arbitrary tensor factor N. Tensor with its kernel, cover, and quotient. The middle row is short exact, all rows and columns are right exact, and flatness of the original quotient makes the third vertical map monic. Successive epic refinements lift a kernel element into the middle row and then into the kernel row; cancellation of the middle-row monomorphism proves injectivity after tensoring with N. Combine this with right exactness to obtain termwise short exactness.

source.place: Tag 0G7B, lemma-K-flat-two-out-of-three-ses; Modules on Sites Tag 03EX, lemma-flat-tor-zero

proof.text: For each total degree n, form the discrete diagram indexed by pairs (p,q) with p+q=n of these short exact sequences. Prove short exactness in the functor category componentwise, then apply its colimit functor. The latter is exact: transfer exact coproducts of abelian groups to abelian sheaves by exact sheafification, and then to module sheaves by their forgetful functor to abelian sheaves, which preserves coproducts and finite limits and reflects isomorphisms. The coproducts are exactly the degree-n objects of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Check the induced maps on every coproduct injection using HomologicalComplex.ι_mapBifunctorMap. Hence the mapped sequence under tensorRight with any complex is short exact. This is the existing direct-sum total complex with its differential, without any new chain maps or boundedness assumptions.

source.place: Tag 0G7B, lemma-K-flat-two-out-of-three-ses; Modules on Sites Tag 03EX, lemma-flat-tor-zero

proof.text: Transport the short exact total-tensor sequence through the natural braiding isomorphism tensorLeft A ≅ tensorRight A, supplied by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. This proves the left-tensor version needed by [def-pc-kflat-complex], while the right-tensor version is the first conjunct of the theorem.

source.place: Tag 0G7B, lemma-K-flat-two-out-of-three-ses; Modules on Sites Tag 03EX, lemma-flat-tor-zero

proof.text: For any acyclic test A, use [def-pc-kflat-complex] to make the two known tensors acyclic. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact], use the exact segments H^n(K)→H^n(P)→H^{n+1}(L), H^n(L)→H^n(K)→H^n(P), and H^{n-1}(P)→H^n(L)→H^n(K) for the three conclusions respectively. Both outer terms vanish, so the middle cohomology object is zero. By [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules] the third tensor is acyclic in every degree. Quantify over all acyclic tests to conclude all three K-flatness implications.
